fNIRS signal predictive of connectivity change after active iTBS

description.value: A randomized sham-controlled intervention study linking fNIRS oxy-Hb responses during intermittent theta-burst stimulation with resting-state fMRI functional-connectivity changes in patients with depression.

spans.text: To understand the network effects behind such a prefrontal fNIRS response during rTMS, and to test whether the fNIRS signal may be predictive of treatment response, we linked data from fNIRS and fMRI within a clinical intervention study.

value: there were no a-priori hypotheses; all analyses were explorative

spans.text: Given the novel approach of linking findings from the two neuroimaging modalities, i.e., fNIRS and fMRI, all analyses were explorative and there were no a-priori hypotheses.

description.value: Randomized, sham-controlled, parallel-group clinical intervention study. Patients received active or sham iTBS twice daily for ten days; fNIRS was acquired during treatment and fMRI at baseline and follow-up.

Given the novel approach of linking findings from the two neuroimaging modalities, i.e., fNIRS and fMRI, all analyses were explorative and there were no a-priori hypotheses.

For first-level analyses, seed-to-voxel functional connectivity analysis was performed for each patient’s baseline and follow-up scan in CONN, and the resulting connectivity correlation values were transformed using Fisher’s r-to-z transformation.
This resulted in 17 patients in the active iTBS group, and 17 patients in the sham iTBS group included in the analysis.
